answer: Attention-rent trellis. Each identity must occupy a public queue slot for a fixed dwell window before any action counts, enforced by a scheduler that only advances agents whose prior slot was fully consumed. A sybil must therefore fund parallel dwell across a tundra of idle slots, multiplying its latency and compute cost per fake identity by the window length. One raven can watch many slots but cannot shorten them, so the attacker's per-identity cost scales with total concurrent attention, not with a one-time payment.
